title: Petroleum Geology
description: Oil is cooked: buried mud full of dead plankton warms as it sinks, and the kerogen in it breaks down. Too cool and it stays solid shale; in the oil window, about 60 to 120 °C held for millions of years, it gives oil; hotter, only gas; hotter still, nothing. Lopatin added it up as a time temperature index, the rate doubling every ten degrees. Then the oil must flow to a trap through the pores of the rock, by Darcy's law. Adds the oil window to the Deep Drilling Rig; oil shale, tar sands, asphalt lakes and cold seeps lie in the Overworld, and the Overcooked Depths in the Planetary Interior.

puzzle.goal: Oil of viscosity μ flows through rock of permeability k and cross section A, pushed by a pressure drop Δp over a length L. Write the flow Q (Darcy).
puzzle.name: Darcy's law
puzzle.ask: Find Q in m³/s for k = 1e-13 m², A = 100 m², Δp = @{dp} Pa, μ = 0.005 Pa·s and L = 500 m.
puzzle.method: Like current through a resistor: flow is proportional to the push and the area, against the viscosity and the length.
